blocks.prompt: 3. Differentiate with respect to the variable involved: \(y = x\sec x + \frac{1}{x}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yahan \(y\) do terms ka jama hai: pehli term \(x\sec x\) ek product hai, doosri \(\frac{1}{x}\) \(x\) ki power hai.
Diya kya hai? \(y = x\sec x + \frac{1}{x}\). Find kya karna hai? \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Rule kaunsa? Sum rule se har term ka derivative alag alag lenge: pehli par product rule, doosri par power rule.
Plan: \(\frac{1}{x}\) ko \(x^{-1}\) likhenge taa ke power rule seedha lag sake, phir dono derivatives jama karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = x\sec x + \frac{1}{x}\).
Maloom karna: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: jama wale function ka derivative har hisse ke derivative ka jama hota hai (sum rule). Pehla hissa product hai, to product rule; doosra power hai, to power rule.

Sum rule se torein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{d}{dx}(x\sec x) + \dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{-1})\]
Kyun: sum rule. Saath hi \(\frac{1}{x}\) ko \(x^{-1}\) likha, kyunke power rule \(x^n\) wali shakal par hi lagta hai.

Pehli term par product rule
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(x\sec x) = (1)\sec x + x\sec x\tan x\]
Kyun: \(u = x\), \(v = \sec x\). \((x)' = 1\), aur \((\sec x)' = \sec x\tan x\), jo humne Question 1(a) mein khud derive kiya tha.

Doosri term par power rule
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{-1}) = -x^{-2} = -\dfrac{1}{x^2}\]
Kyun: \((x^n)' = nx^{n-1}\), yahan \(n = -1\), to power ek kam ho kar \(-2\) ho gayi aur aage \(-1\) aa gaya.
Dhyan dein: \(-1 - 1 = -2\) hota hai, \(0\) nahi. Negative power mein ek kam karna yani aur negative hona.

Sab jama karein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sec x + x\sec x\tan x - \dfrac{1}{x^2}\]
\[= \sec x(1 + x\tan x) - \dfrac{1}{x^2}\]
Kyun: pehli do terms mein \(\sec x\) common hai, usay bahar nikala. Dono shaklein sahi hain.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \pi:\ \sec\pi(1 + 0) - \dfrac{1}{\pi^2} = -1 - \dfrac{1}{\pi^2}\]
Kyun: \(x = \pi\) ke qareeb \(\sec x\) taqreeban \(-1\) hai, to \(y\) taqreeban \(-x + \frac{1}{x}\) jaisa hai, jis ka slope \(-1 - \frac{1}{x^2}\) hai. Dono baatein milti hain.
blocks.final_answer: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \sec x + x\sec x\tan x - \frac{1}{x^2} = \sec x(1 + x\tan x) - \frac{1}{x^2}\)
